{{Short description|Unsolved problem in topology}}
{{about|mathematician Sergei Novikov's topology conjecture|astrophysicist Igor Novikov's conjecture regarding time travel|Novikov self-consistency principle}}

The '''Novikov conjecture''' is one of the most important [[open problem|unsolved problems]] in [[topology]].  It is named for [[Sergei Novikov (mathematician)|Sergei Novikov]] who originally posed the [[conjecture]] in 1965.

The Novikov conjecture concerns the [[homotopy]] invariance of certain [[polynomial]]s in the [[Pontryagin class]]es of a [[manifold]], arising from the [[fundamental group]]. According to the Novikov conjecture, the ''higher signatures'', which are certain numerical invariants of [[smooth manifold]]s, are homotopy invariants.

The conjecture has been [[mathematical proof|proved]] for [[finitely generated abelian group]]s. It is not yet known whether the Novikov conjecture holds true for all [[group (mathematics)|group]]s.  There are no known [[counterexample]]s to the conjecture.

==Precise formulation of the conjecture==

Let <math>G</math> be a [[discrete group]] and <math>BG</math> its [[classifying space]], which is an [[Eilenberg–MacLane space]] of type <math>K(G,1)</math>, and therefore unique up to [[homotopy equivalence]] as a [[CW complex]]. Let

:<math>f\colon M\rightarrow BG</math>

be a continuous map from a closed oriented <math>n</math>-dimensional manifold <math>M</math> to <math>BG</math>, and

:<math>x \in H^{n-4i} (BG;\mathbb{Q} ).</math>

Novikov considered the numerical expression, found by evaluating the cohomology class in top dimension against the [[fundamental class]] <math>[M]</math>, and known as a '''higher signature''':

:<math>\left\langle f^*(x) \cup L_i(M),[M] \right\rangle \in \mathbb{Q}</math>

where <math>L_i</math> is the <math>i^{\rm th}</math> [[Hirzebruch polynomial]], or sometimes (less descriptively) as the <math>i^{\rm th}</math> <math>L</math>-polynomial. For each <math>i</math>, this polynomial can be expressed in the Pontryagin classes of the manifold's [[tangent bundle]]. The '''Novikov conjecture''' states that the higher signature is an invariant of the oriented homotopy type of <math>M</math> for every such map <math>f</math> and every such class <math>x</math>, in other words, if <math>h\colon M' \rightarrow M</math> is an orientation preserving homotopy equivalence, the higher signature associated to <math>f \circ h</math> is equal to that associated to <math>f</math>.

==Connection with the Borel conjecture==

The Novikov conjecture is equivalent to the rational injectivity of the [[assembly map]] in [[L-theory]]. The 
[[Borel conjecture]] on the rigidity of aspherical manifolds is equivalent to the assembly map being an [[isomorphism]].
